prompt_en:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: original single-canvas subculture narrative illustration
Primary request: Depict one adult night mender completing the final handoff before closing inside a worn memory-repair workshop. First glance: one adult night mender reaches across the counter with a repaired, heavily worn coat while one anonymous recipient hand enters the closing doorway, frozen a finger-width before contact. At the decisive instant, the one adult mender extends the repaired coat while the recipient's cropped hand stops a finger-width short of contact. The visible actor is the adult night mender. The directed action is extending the repaired coat across the counter. The visible target is the repaired coat held toward the approaching recipient hand. The visible consequence is that the taut thread pulls the last loose cuff seam shut as the closing bell begins to tilt. Keep the adult mender's extending hand, the repaired coat cuff, the approaching recipient hand, and the single crimson thread as one high-contrast diagonal focal path.
Second look: the brass threshold and receiving mat already register the coat's arrival before the real handoff is complete. At the focal consequence, the same thread leaves the newly closed cuff as one broad pale seam and enters the clear brass threshold strip beneath the closing doorway. The pale luminous seam crosses the brass threshold before the real handoff is complete. Reserve the unoccupied receiving mat below the doorway as a clear, empty secondary clue surface containing one broad dry coat-length patch. Rain beads stop at a broad dry coat-length boundary on the unoccupied receiving mat. Matching crescent abrasions on the coat cuff, the mender's leather thimble, the counter edge, and a repaired stool leg show that every repair happened through the same long working history. Beyond the threshold seam, the dark closing doorway withholds the recipient and leaves the next destination recoverable only from the material trail.
The familiar anchor is one adult night mender completing the final handoff before closing. The governing changed rule is that the single thread changes physical state whenever memory crosses from hand to tool, garment, or room. Use one-beat-ahead memory seam as the sole repeatable signature. A taut crimson fiber wraps the mender's needle fingers and enters the coat cuff. The same crimson thread loosens into translucent memory loops inside one clear glass bobbin. The same thread hardens into a luminous repaired seam across the worn cuff and then thins into the counter groove and threshold. Repeat only one motif family—the single crimson memory thread—through the mender's fingers, glass bobbin, repaired cuff, counter groove, and threshold, changing its physical state at each transfer.
Use firm dark ink edges only around the mender's extending hand, the recipient's cropped hand, the coat cuff, the needle, and the crimson thread; reduce tools to softer lines and let peripheral shelves break into dry, unfinished strokes. Let rear shelves, ceiling corners, and the far floor dissolve into quiet paper grain with incomplete marks. Leave the door's darkness and outer shelves as silent negative space, hiding the next event while preserving the thread's threshold direction. Stage the handoff as large simple masses within the central canvas so it reads at 320 pixels, and keep the crimson route continuous and traceable from hand through tool and garment into the environment. Preserve one decisive instant, one fully visible adult actor, and no duplicated figure or timeline echo. No readable text, captions, labels, logos, named style, protected design, or franchise element.
negative_en: named artist or studio imitation, protected character or franchise copy, franchise logo, readable generated title text, random symbol stack, universal color or shape stereotype, aspect-ratio-only composition, unclear actor-action-target relation, equal-detail clutter, static character lineup, lore exposition text
